Add Neighborhood Cell-Type Composition to a NICHESObject

Source: R/add_neighborhood_composition.R
add_neighborhood_composition.Rd

For each cell, counts how many neighbors of each cell type fall within its local neighborhood. Neighborhood membership is derived directly from $edge.list: cell B is considered a neighbor of cell A if any directed edge connects them (regardless of direction). Counts are zero-filled against the full dataset's cell type universe so that every cell has a value for every type.

Usage

add_neighborhood_composition(
  niches.obj,
  cell.type.col = NULL,
  include.self = TRUE,
  normalize = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

niches.obj

A NICHESObject with mode = "spatial".

cell.type.col

Character. Name of the column in $cell.meta holding cell type annotations. Hard error if NULL or not found.

include.self

Logical. Whether to count the focal cell itself as one of its own neighbors. Default TRUE. When TRUE, cell A contributes 1 to its own type's count regardless of whether an autocrine self-loop edge exists.

normalize

Logical. When TRUE (default), also produces <PolishedType>.neighbor.prop columns: each count divided by the total number of neighbors (including self when include.self = TRUE). Proportions sum to 1 per cell; cells with zero neighbors receive 0.

verbose

Logical. Emit progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

The input niches.obj with $aggregations$neighborhood.composition populated or replaced.

Details

The result is stored as a single data.table at $aggregations$neighborhood.composition, replacing any previously computed version unconditionally.

Column naming

Cell type labels are sanitized for use as column names via gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9.]", ".", type), which replaces spaces, slashes, parentheses, and other special characters with dots. The resulting columns follow the pattern <PolishedType>.neighbor.count (and optionally <PolishedType>.neighbor.prop). Columns are ordered alphabetically by polished type name. For example, cell type "CD8+ T cell" becomes "CD8..T.cell.neighbor.count".

Spatial mode only

This function raises a hard error when attr(niches.obj, "mode") == "nonspatial". In nonspatial mode, edges are statistically paired rather than spatially proximate, so neighborhood composition would reflect sampling design rather than local tissue structure. This is biologically meaningless and is therefore not supported.

Double-counting prevention

Because spatial graphs are typically bidirectional (edges A->B and B->A both exist for proximate cells), the neighbor set for each focal cell is formed as the union of all cells appearing on the other end of any edge, deduplicated before counting. Each physical neighbor is counted exactly once regardless of how many directed edges connect them.

See also

add_neighborhood_edge_agg, add_neighborhoods, aggregate_NICHESObject

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_example)

obj <- add_neighborhood_composition(
  NICHESv2_example,
  cell.type.col = "celltype"
)
#> [add_neighborhood_composition] Computing composition across 80 cells | 3 cell types ...
#> [add_neighborhood_composition] Done. 80 cells | 3 cell types | columns: count + prop.
head(obj$aggregations$neighborhood.composition)
#> Key: <cell>
#>       cell TypeA.neighbor.count TypeB.neighbor.count TypeC.neighbor.count
#>     <char>                <int>                <int>                <int>
#> 1:  Cell_1                    5                    0                    0
#> 2: Cell_10                    6                    0                    0
#> 3: Cell_11                    6                    0                    0
#> 4: Cell_12                    4                    0                    0
#> 5: Cell_13                    2                    0                    0
#> 6: Cell_14                    6                    0                    0
#>    TypeA.neighbor.prop TypeB.neighbor.prop TypeC.neighbor.prop
#>                  <num>               <num>               <num>
#> 1:                   1                   0                   0
#> 2:                   1                   0                   0
#> 3:                   1                   0                   0
#> 4:                   1                   0                   0
#> 5:                   1                   0                   0
#> 6:                   1                   0                   0

# Without self-counting and without proportions
obj2 <- add_neighborhood_composition(
  NICHESv2_example,
  cell.type.col = "celltype",
  include.self  = FALSE,
  normalize     = FALSE
)
#> [add_neighborhood_composition] Computing composition across 80 cells | 3 cell types ...
#> [add_neighborhood_composition] Done. 80 cells | 3 cell types | columns: count.
# }
